newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart December store sales up,Circuit City down.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart December store sales up,Circuit City down.

text.p: Two of the nation's biggest retailers reported mixed results Tuesday for December, the latest chains to post lackluster sales for the important holiday selling season.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc, the nation's largest retailer, said December sales rose 6.8 percent at comparable stores, those open at least a year.
Total sales including new stores rose 11.7 percent to $14.13 billion for the five weeks ended on Jan. 3, the Bentonville, Ark.-based retailer said.
Circuit City Stores Inc, a large retailer of consumer electronics and appliances, said comparable store sales fell 13 percent.
December sales including new stores rose four percent to $1.17 billion, the Richmond, Va.-based company said.
Sales of personal computers and other electronic gear were especially disappointing over the holidays, retailers and analysts have said.
"Overall, holiday sales results will be viewed as mildly disappointing," Gruntal & Co retail industry analyst Michael Conn said in a report.
While many chains will meet their conservative holiday sales plans, "expectations going into the holiday season were for strong above-plan results," he wrote.

In another sign that sales were not as strong as retailers had hoped, Telecheck Services, a check clearing company, said that comparable-store sales rose just 0.3 percent in December and 2.4 percent for the holiday season through Dec. 24.
Telecheck had projected a holiday sales increase of 2 percent to 4 percent.
The lackluster results were particularly disappointing given the weak Christmas sales season in 1995.
Toys R Us Inc on Monday reported sluggish holiday sales that it said would hurt 1996 earnings, prompting a 15 percent drop in its stock price.

The world's largest toy retailer said domestic sales rose four percent in December but were flat for all of the holiday season on a comparable-store basis. The late Thanksgiving holiday and a lack of software titles hurt results, it said, despite solid demand for Nintendo 64 video game machines and Tickle Me Elmo dolls.
The traditional holiday season had five fewer selling days since Thanksgiving came later because of the calendar.
Last week J.C. Penney Co. Inc. said comparable-store sales rose 6.2 percent in December and Dayton Hudson Corp. reported a 4.2 percent increase, gains that analysts described as modest.
Wal-Mart stock rose 87.5 cents to $23 and Circuit City stock fell 12.5 cents to $29.375 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
